articles.title: Inside Health - Fake make up: a bargain or a health risk? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Black Friday and Christmas shoppers are warned fake cosmetics can contain toxic chemicals.
articles.body: Shopping in a cost of living crisis means more of us are looking for bargains. But ahead of Black Friday and the Christmas shopping rush, experts are warning consumers to be cautious. Tests on fake make-up, perfumes and skin creams have been shown to contain dangerous substances such as mercury and nicotine. Laura Foster speaks to toxicologist Rani Ghosh and Helen Barnham from the Intellectual Property Office about the health risks linked to fake cosmetics including blistering, blindness and kidney damage. After research by the University of Cambridge and University of East Anglia suggested females with autoimmune diseases are less likely than men to be believed, more and more women have been coming forward to share their experiences. We hear from Beth Smith from East Yorkshire about her long, diagnostic journey and speak to the research lead, Dr Melanie Sloan, about what can be done to stop the gender bias and reduce the likelihood of anyone being misdiagnosed, no matter their gender. Plus, BBC Radio 4 presenter Claudia Hammond pops in to talk about this year’s All in the Mind awards which celebrate people helping others with their mental health. She also shares some of the tips she’s learned from previous winners on how best to support people who are struggling. articles.title: Three easy ways to help you beat the winter blues
articles.summary: It's easy to feel gloomy in winter, but here are three ways to help you manage the darker days and even embrace them.
articles.body:
Now the clocks have gone back and the evenings are darker, many of us are trudging to work and back in the dark and sometimes our mood is lower as well.

We can feel more tired than normal, lack energy or find it difficult to concentrate.

Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD), or " winter depression " can affect anyone. For those struggling to stick to their normal daily activites, the NHS advises contacting their local GP.

For those with milder symptoms, here are three ways to help you manage the darker days and even embrace them.

Psychologist Kari Leibowitz says growing up in the US in a summer-centric town meant she used to view winter as limiting and uncomfortable, but travelling to Norway where some places get almost no daylight in the depths of winter changed her mindset.

She found that instead of people succumbing to a darker mood, they embraced their circumstances, finding different hobbies from snow sports to knitting and cooking.

"They're looking at winter as a time of year that's full of opportunities," she says.

Kari said it taught her that changing your approach to focus on what you can do during this time, rather than what you can't, was surprisingly effective.

This could include winter walks, movie nights, cooking a new meal or ice skating.

"So often we only focus on the things that are harder to do in the winter when really there's a whole world of seasonal activities that feel better when it's cold out."

With our work and social calendars ticking along as normal, we may wonder why we feel so tired but Kari says we need to accept our bodies need more rest in winter.

"It's actually good not to be as productive or active as you would be during the summer months because our bodies are biologically hardwired for rest during winter," she says.

Just like animals and plants, she says we should be slowing down and changing our behaviour.

Dr Em May Armstrong, a plant researcher, says the key is finding the balance between resting more and becoming too lethargic.

She suggests so called "active dormancy" - mixing a slower restful lifestyle with activities that still keep us mentally engaged.

This could include activities such as knitting, repairing clothes or practices that help get you ready for the year ahead.

"And while that's not as active as, say, travelling or camping, it's just as active in a more restorative way."

While resting more is natural, it is still important to make time for the things that make us happy and to mix with other people, according to GP Gavin Francis.

"We're very social animals, even the most solitary human being doesn't live completely alone. We all depend on others."

He suggests planning activities in advance, focusing on spending time with those who make you feel good, and activities which can boost your mood.

Doing this means you're committed, and a low mood nearer the time won't be able to stop you.

"You can then start planning in your diary to do more things with these people over winter," he says.

Simple practical things to improve your mood, such as making sure you get a good night's sleep, avoiding too much alcohol or late night parties and maintaining a healthy diet are also important, he says.

"These things are not rocket science, but they're really fundamental to having a good, healthy circadian rhythm and a good healthy physiology through the winter."

articles.title: Iranian leaders fret over public mood as gas shortages add to war ills
articles.summary: By Parisa Hafezi and Melory Ghazi DUBAI, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Iran shows no sign of making concessions in the war with the US, but its warnings to citizens of...
articles.body:
A street food wendor works, amid a gas shortage, in Tehran

DUBAI, Nov 16 (Reuters) - Iran shows no sign of making concessions in the war with the US, but its warnings to citizens of gas shortages this winter are the latest sign of its own vulnerabilities in the conflict, with its ports blockaded and infrastructure hammered ‌by US strikes.

The government said last week that, though Iran has had gas shortages before, they would be more severe this winter because of war damage ‌to processing plants and most regions would be affected.

Toiling under the effects of a war that has intensified rampant inflation and destroyed millions of jobs, Iranians face growing hardships that senior figures fear will deepen divisions ​still raw from the crushing of mass protests last winter.

"The reality is that if our gas gets cut off, we'll have to close down and go home," said Seyyed Ahmad Seyyedi, a street vendor.

"This war must end so that we can return to normal life and all the problems and high prices can come to an end. Continuing life under these conditions is difficult," said Mina Lahrasabi, 65, who works in a rice factory near Iran's Caspian coast.

A senior Iranian official and an Iranian security official told Reuters the country's hierarchy was increasingly concerned about ‌the situation, with the internal fuel shortage adding to worries ⁠of public unrest.

There have been no notable protests against the ruling system since the war began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, but domestic intelligence agencies were on alert, the security official said.

The agencies were closely monitoring ⁠for any sign of opposition and believed the US might seek to provoke street demonstrations, the security official added.

The senior official warned that the increasingly difficult living standards faced by the Iranian population were getting harder for people to withstand, describing it as a fire smouldering beneath ashes.

"This is the most severe siege imposed on us since the revolution," said Iranian analyst Saeed Leylaz.

At a ​heater ​company in Tehran, salesman Amin Sha'bani said the prospect of a cold winter was concerning – and that ​customers were increasingly considering electric products rather than gas, though both were ‌often now too expensive for customers.

"Given what has happened in the past nine months, with power plants attacked, it's perfectly natural to worry that the weather will get colder," he said.

Although Iran is a major gas producer controlling part of the world's biggest gas field, it has sometimes been unable to meet domestic consumption because of outdated equipment, a problem worsened by international sanctions.

Government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said last week that the gas shortage this winter would likely be 430 million cubic metres, compared to 300 million last year.

Iran's national gas company has blamed the worsening shortage on damage to four processing plants early in the war, which it says it is trying to fix.

However, the senior Iranian official told ‌Reuters measures being taken to resolve the problem only amounted to short-term fixes and said there had ​been numerous meetings to try to manage the looming crisis for the winter.

A second senior Iranian source ​said Iran was in talks to import gas from Russia.

"This could become a ​critical issue, but measures have been taken and we will get through it," said Leylaz, the analyst. "In the worst-case scenario, we may have to ‌cut gas supplies to industries for a period, but we have ​not reached that point yet."

That more sanguine view ​was held by several Iranians Reuters reached inside the country by messaging app.

Reza, a 45-year-old in Urmia in the northwest of Iran, where the winters can bring heavy snowfall, said there was little concern among people he knew about the potential shortages and that his family had bought three electric heaters in case.

Iran has also ​suffered periodic power blackouts in recent years.

"The reality is that ‌I don't mean to start crying now over what might happen. We already have enough problems – inflation, high prices and other difficulties to see a ​potential fuel shortage as relatively minor," said Zahra Hosseini, 44, who works for a food company in Tabriz.

(Reporting by Parisa Hafezi and Melory Ghazi; additional ​reporting by Bahareh Khodabandeh and Emily Giles; Writing by Angus McDowall; Editing by Alex Richardson)

articles.title: Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo is undergoing care after eating a hat that got into enclosure
articles.summary: CINCINNATI (AP) — The Cincinnati Zoo says its beloved hippo Fiona, who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — The Cincinnati Zoo says its beloved hippo Fiona , who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat that got into her enclosure.

Zoo veterinarians and staff are monitoring Fiona and working to help her pass the hat, the zoo said in a statement Monday.

"Her care team is cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self," the zoo said.

The cap got into Fiona's habitat after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a small opening above the area's viewing windows, said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.

Fiona was born six weeks premature in January 2017, and her fight to survive grabbed international attention.

She initially couldn't stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds (13.2 kilograms) at birth, 25 pounds (11.3 kilograms) less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

Fans followed her progress online, and she became so popular that books were written about her. She also inspired a line of beer, all sorts of clothing and an ice cream flavor.

One couple even got engaged in front of her exhibit, with Fiona getting into the picture while underwater in the background.

articles.title: EUA confirmam investigação sobre a Megaspeed por suposto desvio de chips para a China | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Departamento de Comércio, a investigação foi aberta em 2024 para verificar se a empresa descumpriu as regras americanas de exportação.
articles.summary: Segundo o Departamento de Comércio, a investigação foi aberta em 2024 para verificar se a empresa descumpriu as regras americanas de exportação.
articles.body:
O governo dos Estados Unidos confirmou uma investigação sobre o grupo Megaspeed, de Singapura, por supostamente ajudar empresas chinesas a contornar as restrições americanas à exportação de chips.

Em um comunicado conjunto divulgado na noite de segunda-feira (16), os departamentos de Comércio e da Justiça afirmam que estão trabalhando para "aplicar todo o peso da lei contra a Megaspeed por qualquer atividade criminosa que possa ter ocorrido".

Segundo o comunicado, o Departamento de Comércio abriu uma investigação sobre a Megaspeed em 2024 para verificar se a empresa descumpriu regras de exportação dos Estados Unidos.

A nota também destacou que a investigação foi iniciada após "uma inspeção presencial nas instalações da Megaspeed para verificar o uso final dos produtos em junho de 2025".

Durante a inspeção, as autoridades interrogaram a então CEO Alice Huang, acusada pelos serviços de inteligência dos Estados Unidos de espionagem para a China.

A revelação da relação de Huang com o então CEO da Nvidia , Jensen Huang, provocou a renúncia deste último na semana passada.

articles.title: Spray de pimenta gratuito em Belém: veja como mulheres podem obter | G1
articles.standfirst: Item de defesa pessoal é entregue após preenchimento de formulário e capacitação obrigatória. Veja detalhes.
articles.summary: A Prefeitura de Belém oferece spray de pimenta gratuito para defesa pessoal de mulheres acima de 18 anos após capacitação obrigatória.
articles.body:
Mulheres que querem se equipar com um spray de pimenta como método de defesa pessoal já podem fazer a retirada de forma gratuita em Belém .

Para receber o equipamento, é preciso preencher um formulário e passar por uma capacitação. Só depois dessa etapa a mulher fica apta a levar o spray, de acordo com a prefeitura da capital.

O governo federal sancionou em julho a lei que libera a venda e posse de aerossóis de extratos vegetais , como spray de pimenta, para mulheres acima de 18 anos como medida de defesa pessoal .

Nesta quinta-feira (12), uma ação de enfrentamento à violência contra a mulher foi promovida pela Secretaria Executiva de Políticas Públicas e Bem-Estar Social (Sepes) em uma escola pública no bairro da Marambaia. Foram distribuídos mais de 30 sprays de pimenta para estudantes atendidas pela iniciativa.

A iniciativa buscou fortalecer a segurança, a autonomia e a confiança das mulheres, especialmente daquelas que já enfrentaram situações de violência. Além da entrega dos equipamentos, a ação abriu espaço para o diálogo sobre os diferentes tipos de violência e a importância de reconhecer os primeiros sinais de um relacionamento abusivo.

Mulheres interessadas em ter um spray de pimenta podem procurar a sede da Secretaria Executiva de Políticas Públicas e Bem-Estar Social (Sepes), na avenida Nazaré, 361 , em frente ao clube Paysandu, em Belém.

articles.title: Inovação no Piauí: estado sobe 11 posições e lidera avanço no país | G1
articles.standfirst: Os dados são do Índice de Inovação dos Estados 2026, elaborado pela Fiec. O estado passou da 26ª colocação em 2022 para a 15ª em 2026.
articles.summary: Com avanços em sustentabilidade e instituições, a inovação no Piauí saltou 11 posições no ranking nacional da Fiec, registrando a maior evolução de todo o país.
articles.body:
Empregos em indústria do Piauí. — Foto: Regis Falcão

O Piauí foi o estado que mais avançou em inovação no Brasil nos últimos cinco anos, segundo o Índice de Inovação dos Estados 2026. O estado subiu 11 posições no ranking nacional, passando do 26º lugar, em 2022, para o 15º, em 2026.

O levantamento é elaborado pela Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Ceará (Fiec) e considera fatores como qualificação profissional, infraestrutura, pesquisa e ambiente institucional para avaliar a capacidade de inovação das unidades da federação.

O indicador avalia as condições oferecidas pelos estados para o desenvolvimento de novas tecnologias, negócios e pesquisas.

Entre os critérios analisados estão a qualificação dos profissionais, a infraestrutura, os investimentos em ciência e tecnologia e o ambiente institucional.

Além do avanço em capacidades de inovação, o Piauí ficou na 20ª posição no ranking geral de inovação do Brasil e na 7ª colocação entre os estados do Nordeste.

O levantamento reúne indicadores relacionados à inovação, à competitividade e ao desenvolvimento tecnológico. A avaliação considera tanto as condições que os estados oferecem para inovar quanto os resultados alcançados nessas áreas.

Entre os destaques do Piauí está o indicador de Instituições, no qual o estado ocupa a 9ª posição nacional. Esse quesito avalia aspectos como a eficiência dos serviços públicos, a capacidade de arrecadação e gestão financeira do estado e o uso de tecnologias digitais na administração pública.

O Piauí foi o estado que mais avançou em inovação no Brasil nos últimos cinco anos, segundo o Índice de Inovação dos Estados 2026. — Foto: Reprodução

O Piauí também aparece entre os dez melhores estados em Sustentabilidade Ambiental, com a 8ª colocação. Nesse indicador, são considerados fatores como a geração de energia renovável, as certificações ambientais e os investimentos em gestão ambiental.

Outro destaque é o avanço em Propriedade Intelectual. Nos últimos cinco anos, o estado subiu cinco posições nesse indicador e registrou o maior crescimento do país. A avaliação considera registros de patentes, marcas, desenhos industriais e contratos de pesquisa.

articles.title: RN sobe para 14º lugar em ranking nacional de inovação | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado avançou cinco posições no indicador que mede as condições para inovar, mas caiu três lugares na dimensão que avalia os resultados.
articles.summary: Com avanço na formação profissional, o Rio Grande do Norte sobe para 14º em inovação, mas enfrenta desafios em competitividade e resultados práticos no mercado.
articles.body:
Supercomputador da UFRN, no Núcleo de Processamento de Alto Desempenho — Foto: Cícero Oliveira/UFRN

O Rio Grande do Norte subiu da 15ª para a 14ª posição no ranking nacional de inovação entre 2025 e 2026, mas apresentou resultados diferentes nas duas dimensões que compõem a avaliação. Enquanto avançou cinco posições no Índice de Capacidades, passando do 21º para o 16º lugar, o estado caiu da 9ª para a 12ª colocação no Índice de Resultados.

Os dados são da oitava edição do Índice de Inovação dos Estados, desenvolvido pelo Observatório da Indústria Ceará, do Sistema Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Ceará (FIEC), em parceria com a Confederação Nacional da Indústria (CNI). O levantamento avalia as 27 unidades da Federação e as cinco regiões brasileiras. No Nordeste, o RN ocupa a quarta posição.

🔎 Diferença entre os dois índices: o de Capacidades avalia os fatores que criam condições para a inovação, como formação profissional, infraestrutura e investimentos em instituições. Já o de Resultados mede o desempenho com base em aspectos como produção científica, empreendedorismo, propriedade intelectual e sustentabilidade ambiental.

A classificação geral considera os dois conjuntos de indicadores. Na edição de 2026, o RN alcançou índice de 0,194 e ficou em 14º lugar. A escala utilizada pelo estudo permite comparar o desempenho dos estados em cada dimensão e indicador.

O levantamento também mostra que o RN ocupa posições distintas entre os 12 indicadores específicos. Os melhores resultados aparecem em Sustentabilidade Ambiental, na qual o estado está em 6º lugar, Capital Humano – Graduação, em 9º, Capital Humano – Pós-Graduação e Produção Científica, ambos em 10º.

Na outra ponta, os principais pontos de atenção são Instituições, com o 23º lugar, e Competitividade Global, na 21ª posição.

Entre os 12 indicadores, o melhor resultado potiguar é em Sustentabilidade Ambiental, com a 6ª colocação nacional. O estado também aparece entre os dez primeiros em Capital Humano – Graduação (9º), Capital Humano – Pós-Graduação (10º) e Produção Científica (10º).

Os resultados mostram um desempenho melhor em áreas relacionadas à formação de profissionais e à produção de conhecimento. Por outro lado, a 23ª posição em Instituições e a 21ª em Competitividade Global indicam pontos de atenção.

Desempenho detalhado do Rio Grande do Norte — Foto: FIEC/Divulgação

Na comparação entre 2022 e 2026, o RN também apresentou avanços em indicadores específicos. Segundo o estudo, Capital Humano – Graduação, Investimento e Financiamento Público em Ciência e Tecnologia e Empreendedorismo ganharam oito posições cada um no ranking nacional.

O levantamento também aponta evolução em Inserção de Mestres e Doutores e Intensidade Tecnológica e Criativa.

Para o economista-chefe do Sistema FIEC e gerente do Observatório da Indústria Ceará, Guilherme Muchale, os avanços refletem melhorias na qualificação profissional, na absorção de mão de obra pelo mercado de trabalho e nos investimentos públicos.

“A melhoria nos indicadores mostra que o Rio Grande do Norte vem avançando em uma base sólida para sustentar o processo inovador local, aliando práticas sustentáveis ao compromisso com a disponibilidade e a absorção, pelo mercado de trabalho, de profissionais mais qualificados”, avalia.

O Índice de Inovação dos Estados organiza a avaliação em duas dimensões: Capacidades e Resultados. Cada uma reúne seis indicadores, que, por sua vez, são divididos em 28 subindicadores. A metodologia considera dados de diferentes fontes e áreas para construir um diagnóstico dos ecossistemas de inovação estaduais.

Essa dimensão reúne fatores que favorecem o desenvolvimento da inovação. É uma avaliação da estrutura e dos recursos disponíveis para que empresas, universidades, centros de pesquisa e governos desenvolvam novas soluções.

No RN, o índice passou do 21º para o 16º lugar. Entre os seis indicadores avaliados estão:

Capital Humano – Graduação : considera a formação de profissionais em áreas tecnológicas, como ciência, tecnologia, engenharia e matemática, além da qualidade dos cursos de graduação.

Capital Humano – Pós-Graduação: avalia a formação de profissionais em cursos de pós-graduação.

Inserção de Mestres e Doutores: mede a presença de profissionais com mestrado e doutorado em setores como indústria, tecnologia da informação e comunicação, pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação.

Investimento e Financiamento Público em Ciência e Tecnologia: considera os investimentos públicos em ciência e tecnologia e o financiamento destinado à inovação.

Infraestrutura: reúne aspectos relacionados à estrutura disponível para apoiar o desenvolvimento de atividades inovadoras.

Instituições: avalia fatores institucionais relacionados ao ambiente de inovação, incluindo serviços públicos e capacidade fiscal.

A dimensão de Resultados avalia os efeitos do processo de inovação. O objetivo é observar o que os estados conseguem produzir e transformar em atividade econômica, conhecimento, tecnologia e práticas sustentáveis.

O RN caiu da 9ª para a 12ª posição nessa dimensão. Os seis indicadores são:

Competitividade Global: avalia a inserção dos estados no comércio exterior de produtos de maior intensidade tecnológica e a diversificação de mercados.

Empreendedorismo: considera aspectos relacionados à criação e ao desenvolvimento de negócios inovadores.

Produção Científica: mede a produção de conhecimento científico.

Intensidade Tecnológica e Criativa: avalia a participação de empregos formais em setores de média e alta intensidade tecnológica e em atividades criativas.

Propriedade Intelectual: considera registros e ativos relacionados à proteção de inovações.

Sustentabilidade Ambiental: reúne indicadores ligados ao desempenho ambiental.

articles.title: Homem armado é detido após ameaçar pessoas na Praia de Iracema | G1
articles.standfirst: Após ser capturado, o suspeito foi encaminhado ao hospital para retirada dos dardos do dispositivo. Em seguida, ele foi levada à delegacia.
articles.summary: Agentes da Guarda Municipal usaram um dispositivo elétrico incapacitante para conter o suspeito.
articles.body:
Um homem em posse de uma faca foi contido por agentes da Guarda Municipal por meio do uso de uma arma de choque após ameaçar atentar contra a própria vida e a de outras pessoas no calçadão da Praia de Iracema, em Fortaleza , na madrugada desta segunda-feira (16).

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, a equipe foi acionada após uma testemunha procurar a Base de Segurança Cidadã da Praia de Iracema para denunciar a ação do suspeito.

Através das câmeras de videomonitoramento, os guardas monitoraram o indivíduo, que apareceu em vários momentos de arma em punho . Posteriormente, os guardas realizaram a abordagem.

Diante da negativa do homem em soltar a faca, além do risco para a equipe e pedestres da região, um dos guardas utilizou um dispositivo elétrico incapacitante , conhecido como "Spark" , para conter a ameaça.

"O homem foi atingido no peito e encaminhado a uma unidade hospitalar, conforme procedimento de segurança adotado para a retirada dos dardos do dispositivo", disse a Guarda Municipal.

Após o atendimento médico, a ocorrência foi apresentada ao 2º Distrito Policial.

articles.title: Alta Mogiana tem saca de café arrematada por R$ 110 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Leilão aconteceu durante 5º Seminário Nossa Cafeicultura da Cocapec: Valor será destinado para tratamento do câncer.
articles.summary: Leilão aconteceu durante 5º Seminário Nossa Cafeicultura da Cocapec: Valor será destinado para tratamento do câncer.
articles.body:
Alta Mogiana tem saca de café arrematada por R$ 110 mil — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

A Cocapec realizou nesta quarta-feira, dia 4, o 5º Seminário Nossa Cafeicultura. O evento reuniu mais de 500 famílias em um encontro que debateu os desafios climáticos, a profissionalização da sucessão familiar e o mercado cafeeiro. A noite também marcou a consagração dos cafés de excelência, com a divulgação dos vencedores do Concurso Senhor Café e a realização do leilão solidário.

A cafeicultura brasileira vive um momento em que a tradicional lei da oferta e da procura deixou de ser a única régua da atividade rural. Entre as incertezas dos fenômenos climáticos globais, as exigências ambientais internacionais e a volatilidade dos mercados, a palavra de ordem no campo é profissionalização, tanto nos aspectos mercadológicos quanto na governança da própria família cafeeira.

Esse panorama ditou o ritmo do encontro promovido pela Cocapec. O seminário contou com a participação de quatro importantes nomes da cafeicultura nacional: Simão Pedro de Lima, Gary Amar, André Jacintho Mesquita e Rogério Otaviano de Souza.

Indústria otimista e a força da Alta Mogiana

Apesar dos contratempos climáticos, o horizonte traçado pelas indústrias parceiras é de resiliência e valorização. O representante do Grupo 3Corações, Rogério Otaviano de Souza, destacou que o mercado de café acumula anos consecutivos de preços que remuneram o produtor e que a maturidade da cadeia é evidente.

“O cafeicultor aprendeu a gerenciar suas vendas de forma mais assertiva e a direcionar esforços para nichos de maior valor agregado”, afirmou.

“A região da Alta Mogiana continua sendo um pilar insubstituível para o fornecimento de grãos finos. Cafés para expresso, cápsulas monodose e drip coffee, formatos que eram novidade há uma década, hoje são pilares comerciais consolidados que dependem da consistência dos grãos regionais. Mesmo em safras nas quais as indústrias precisam demonstrar flexibilidade para compor seus blends devido a variações climáticas, o consumo doméstico firme e a demanda externa sustentam um prognóstico promissor”, concluiu.

Durante o seminário, o consultor em governança corporativa Simão Pedro de Lima destacou que a previsibilidade nunca foi uma marca do agronegócio café, mas o cenário atual exige que os produtores olhem para muito além do terreiro.

“Conforme pontuado nas análises técnicas do evento, o setor vem de uma safra ampla, mas agora ingressa no ciclo da bienalidade negativa típica dos anos ímpares, somada à instabilidade trazida pelo El Niño e às floradas irregulares. A colheita recente, marcada por episódios atípicos de chuva, impôs severos desafios de secagem e qualidade. O excesso de umidade elevou o risco de grãos de chão e o surgimento de ocratoxina, demandando ajustes operacionais tanto das propriedades quanto das indústrias processadoras”, ressaltou Simão.

Excelência premiada: confira os ganhadores e os melhores cafés da Alta Mogiana

Durante o 5º Seminário Nossa Cafeicultura, o público pôde conhecer os vencedores do Concurso de Qualidade Senhor Café. Dos mais de 100 inscritos, seis se destacaram na pontuação final.

A busca contínua por excelência, alinhada à força do cooperativismo e aos laços familiares no campo, definiu o tom da premiação que consagrou os melhores cafés da safra. Com pontuações expressivas decididas no detalhe das casas decimais, o Concurso de Qualidade Senhor Café destacou o equilíbrio dos métodos tradicionais e a precisão técnica dos processos de pós-colheita, evidenciando o protagonismo feminino e a vitalidade da sucessão familiar nas lavouras da região.

Categoria Fermentado: ciência, legado e notas acima dos 90 pontos

Na categoria Fermentado, a tecnologia de pós-colheita e o rigor do manejo foram os grandes diferenciais para a obtenção de bebidas com perfis aromáticos complexos e exuberantes.

O lugar mais alto do pódio foi conquistado pela cafeicultora Iara Ceres Oliveira Figueiredo, da Fazenda Areia, localizada em São Tomás de Aquino-MG. Com expressivos 91,33 pontos, o lote consagrou-se como um modelo ideal de fermentação, entregando notas intensas de frutas vermelhas, como morango, framboesa e amora, nuances vínicas, doçura profunda, perfil muito licoroso e finalização persistente.

Após ter alcançado a segunda colocação na edição passada, Iara comemorou o topo ao lado do genro, Fausto, e dos netos:

“O segredo dessa pontuação é muito empenho, pesquisa, estudo e abnegação. Café fermentado requer muito cuidado, preparo e atenção”, destacou a produtora.

Fausto enfatizou a gestão minuciosa da propriedade:

“Fermentar café exige dedicação, estudo e rastreabilidade total da lavoura. Sabemos exatamente o perfil que cada talhão produz”, explicou.

A vitória teve ainda um significado profundamente emocional: a homenagem à memória do Sr. Saulo, marido de Iara, que a partir de 1999 estruturou pioneiramente as lavouras da fazenda com foco em cultivares resistentes e investimento contínuo em irrigação.

O segundo lugar ficou com Henrique Peixoto Rodrigues, de Ibiraci-MG, município que figura entre os maiores polos de café arábica do país e conta com participação ativa de seus cafeicultores junto à cooperativa. Com 90,58 pontos, o café apresentou uma proposta sensorial contrastante e refrescante: perfil dominado por frutas amarelas, com notas de pêssego, abacaxi e limão-siciliano, harmonizando doçura vibrante com acidez cítrica marcante.

A terceira colocação foi garantida pelo jovem cafeicultor David César Faria Bispo, de Pedregulho-SP, alcançando 89,85 pontos. O resultado evidenciou a potência da cafeicultura familiar, alicerçada nos ensinamentos compartilhados entre avós, pais, tios e primos. Na xícara, o lote revelou intensidade de frutas roxas e maduras como ameixa seca, uva-passa e mirtilo, amparadas por uma sensação cremosa, doçura marcante e acidez agradável.

Categoria Natural: a clássica elegância da Alta Mogiana

Entre os cafés da categoria Natural, a harmonia e a doçura tradicional do terroir regional brilharam, premiando lotes de corpo aveludado e equilíbrio sensorial exemplar.

O título de grande campeã foi para a cafeicultora Joana D’Arc Cintra Araujo, acompanhada de seu esposo, Alex, com propriedade em Claraval-MG. Atingindo 89,18 pontos, o lote foi celebrado de forma unânime pelos jurados como a representação legítima do clássico perfil da Alta Mogiana apreciado mundialmente, destacando-se pelas notas refinadas de caramelo, baunilha, chocolate ao leite e avelã, com perfeito balanço entre corpo e cremosidade.

Emocionada com a consagração máxima, Joana declarou:

“Não esperava esse resultado, mas é muito gratificante fazer parte deste momento tão especial em nossas vidas e junto à cooperativa.”

A segunda posição foi obtida pelo produtor Divino de Carvalho Garcia, de Patrocínio Paulista-SP. Com 89,13 pontos, seu café traduziu a excelência da condução da lavoura ao apresentar doçura intensa com notas que remetem a melaço de cana, mel e doce de leite, aliado a um corpo aveludado e equilíbrio impecável.

Encerrando o pódio, a terceira colocação coube à cafeicultora Edna Maria Rodrigues, da tradicional Fazenda Glória, em São José da Bela Vista-SP. Com 89,03 pontos, a bebida chamou atenção pelo perfil aromático delicado, exibindo notas de amêndoas, noz-moscada e jasmim, resultando em uma xícara doce, encorpada e persistente. A propriedade também se destaca pelo cultivo de uvas, demonstrando na prática como o café conversa harmonicamente com outras culturas de valor agregado na mesma terra.

A edição consolida o papel da pesquisa, do cuidado no manejo diário e da união comunitária, mostrando que o futuro dos cafés especiais é construído dia a dia, talhão por talhão, por famílias comprometidas com o mais alto padrão de qualidade.

O ponto alto da noite foi o leilão dos lotes premiados, demonstrando que a alta gastronomia do café caminha lado a lado com a responsabilidade social.

O café campeão de Joana D’Arc, da categoria Natural, atingiu a marca histórica de R$ 110.000,00. Já o lote vencedor da categoria Fermentado teve a saca de 60 quilos arrematada por R$ 45.000,00.

No total geral, o leilão arrecadou expressivos R$ 325.000,00. Seguindo o compromisso solidário da Cocapec, metade do faturamento, exatos R$ 162.500,00, será destinada ao Hospital de Câncer de Passos (MG).

O encerramento do encontro reforçou a essência do cooperativismo: enfrentar os ciclos econômicos de cabeça erguida, promover inovação científica, valorizar a família do campo e retribuir conquistas em benefício de toda a sociedade.

“O 5º Seminário ‘Nossa Cafeicultura’ da Cocapec foi um sucesso e superou nossas expectativas. Mais uma vez, quero agradecer aos nossos cooperados que lotaram o evento. Superamos as previsões no público presente, nas empresas, nos fornecedores, nos clientes e, acima de tudo, na solidariedade. Nosso leilão foi um marco: arrecadamos R$ 325.000,00, dos quais metade irá diretamente para o Hospital de Câncer de Passos. Parabéns aos cooperados, à organização e a todos nós que fazemos da Cocapec essa grande cooperativa. Muito obrigado pela presença de todos”, finalizou Saulo de Carvalho Faleiros, presidente da Cocapec.

articles.title: Inflação do estilo de vida: por que gastamos mais ao ganhar mais? | G1
articles.standfirst: No g1 Explica, a repórter Renata Ribeiro explica e simplifica os temas que dominam o noticiário econômico e mexem diretamente com o nosso bolso.
articles.summary: A inflação do estilo de vida explica por que o aumento de salário muitas vezes não resulta em sobra de dinheiro, pressionado por novos hábitos e custos fixos.
articles.body:
Você já teve um aumento de salário, mas percebeu que, mesmo ganhando mais, o dinheiro continuou sem sobrar no fim do mês? Isso pode acontecer por causa de um fenômeno conhecido como inflação do estilo de vida: à medida que a renda aumenta, os gastos também crescem, muitas vezes sem que a gente perceba.

Com mais dinheiro no bolso, é comum elevar o padrão de consumo, seja frequentando restaurantes mais caros, contratando novos serviços ou fazendo compras que antes não cabiam no orçamento. Aos poucos, o que era um luxo pode virar uma despesa fixa, e o aumento de salário acaba sendo consumido pelos novos hábitos.

Mas não é só uma questão de comportamento. Nos últimos anos, despesas essenciais, como alimentação, plano de saúde, escola e serviços, também pressionaram o orçamento das famílias. Além disso, parcelas de compras e financiamentos comprometem parte da renda, reduzindo o dinheiro disponível no fim do mês.

Toda semana, o g1 Explica descomplica a economia, o mercado financeiro e a educação financeira, mostrando o impacto de tudo isso no seu bolso.

articles.title: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as drone raises alarm at Iraq gas field
articles.summary: Iran reports tanker mine strikes as a drone alert in Iraq and the arrival of a US aircraft carrier raise tensions.
articles.body:
Fresh attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a drone alert at a major gas field in northern Iraq have raised concerns over the security of energy infrastructure across the region, as tensions between the United States and Iran persist despite diplomatic efforts to end their conflict.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Monday that two oil tankers had struck naval mines and caught fire while attempting to cross the southern part of the strait through a route Tehran considers unauthorised.

Separately, Iran’s regular navy said another tanker had caught fire and become immobilised after striking a mine in restricted waters east of the strait.

The claims could not be independently verified, and Iranian authorities did not identify the vessels involved.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency separately reported two tanker attacks in the strait on Monday.

In the latest incident, a tanker was disabled and an engine room fire broke out following an attack seven nautical miles (13km) north of Khasab, Oman.

Earlier, the maritime monitoring agency said another tanker had been struck by an unidentified projectile while travelling out of the strait, also causing an engine room fire. No casualties were reported.

It remained unclear whether either incident was connected to the mine strikes claimed by Iran.

The incidents followed a series of attacks on commercial vessels in recent weeks. The United Nations’ International Maritime Organization recorded 136 security incidents involving vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East between March 1 and November 11, including 35 in October alone.

The threats to maritime energy shipments came as another security alert raised concerns over energy infrastructure elsewhere in the region.

In Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdistan region, warning sirens sounded after a drone flew over the Khor Mor gas field on Monday, Reuters reported, citing two security sources.

There were no immediate reports of a strike or damage from the latest incident.

Production at Khor Mor had already been halted the previous week following a suspected drone attack that sparked a fire and disrupted 2.8 gigawatts of electricity generation, according to United Arab Emirates-based Dana Gas, one of the facility’s operators.

The field is a major source of natural gas for electricity generation in the Kurdish region, making disruptions particularly significant for local power supplies.

It has faced repeated attacks that Iraqi Kurdish officials have blamed on Iranian-backed armed groups.

No group was identified as responsible for Monday’s drone overflight.

The developments came as the US reinforced its military presence in the Middle East, with the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt arriving in the region.

A US official confirmed its arrival to Al Jazeera on Monday, bringing the number of American aircraft carriers operating in the US Central Command area to three, as tensions with Iran remained high and diplomatic efforts to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained stalled.

articles.title: California lifeguard recalls braving relentless waves in rescue caught on video
articles.summary: Days after video captured a San Diego lifeguard defying dangerous surf to save a man in distress, Griffin Houldin recounted the daring rescue.
articles.body: SAN DIEGO — Police run toward the sound of gunfire and firefighters climb up burning buildings, but over the weekend, Griffin Houldin demonstrated what lifeguards do best: He swam undeterred toward a man in distress amid powerful surf off the Southern California coast to make the rescue. Houldin, a 29-year-old San Diego lifeguard, was captured on video swimming toward a struggling man Saturday, taking multiple waves on the head and emerging in whitewater, determined to keep moving. The lifeguard said he didn’t like what he was seeing when the unidentified man hit the water without swim fins and took an unusual line out to sea, so he dove in behind him immediately. The surf, Houldin said in an interview Monday, had doubled in size from late morning to early afternoon, and water was moving around the cove chaotically. “It was heavy,” Houldin said. “It’s a lot of surf, but we train for it, we prepare for it.” The vide shows Houldin displaying impressive athleticism and determination as his red rescue can trails him behind on its tow line. But as he reaches the man, the video captured by visitor Jamie Rea shows, the two did not initially connect. A second attempt, despite the relentless waves, concluded with a solid grab by the swimmer, who held on to the red can through multiple waves. “We got pulled back 5 to 10 feet every wave, and they just kept coming,” Houldin said. “All I was trying to do was stay in this current here and fend off the rocks for as long as possible.” As the swimmer held on to the rescue can, Houldin told him to hold fast. “If he hadn’t been able to hold on, it would have been a very different outcome,” Houldin said. The rescue lasted more than 3 minutes, according to multiple videos. He said the swimmer later told him he misjudged the conditions. Houldin said he would have advised the man not to swim or to at least use swim fins. It was a big day at the cove as the National Weather Service put the Southern California coastline under high surf advisories scheduled to remain in effect through early Wednesday for some beaches. Waves driven by a weekend Pacific storm struck the California coast from north of San Francisco to the U.S.-Mexico border, with waves higher than 30 feet recorded at Mavericks, the noted surf spot in Half Moon Bay, according to the weather service and private wave forecaster Surfline. In Santa Cruz, three surfers were also rescued amid high surf on Saturday, NBC Bay Area reported. Federal forecasters said San Diego beaches would be treated to 6- to 8-foot waves — with some sets reaching 10 feet and beyond. La Jolla Cove isn’t normally a surf spot, but it occasionally breaks in winter, drawing a crowd of surfers and body boarders outside the surf line. San Diego Lifeguard Services, part of the Fire-Rescue Department, completed 175 rescues in the last week, officials said. “It’s dangerous on a normal day, but on a day like Saturday — we haven’t had surf that big in a couple years,” Houldin said. “You can get stuck in that hole, you can get washed up on the cliff here.” Houldin credited fellow lifeguard Cortez Ritumalta for rushing in on a jet ski that ultimately pulled him and the wayward swimmer from the impact zone and toward safety. Both said they have been on the job for more than 10 years. Ritumalta credited onlookers atop the bluffs for pointing him to the rescue in progress. Riding the jet ski on liquid hills amid the foamy aftermath of breaking waves made it hard to see the swimmer, he said Monday. The swimmer was in good hands, though, Ritumalta said, referring to Houldin. “That swimmer probably got the best lifeguard you can have,” he said.

articles.summary: As Eisenkot’s bloc moves to form a government and courts the ultra-Orthodox, Gaza genocide and settler pogroms continue.
articles.body:
Israel’s parliament speaker is due to be replaced on Tuesday, one of several signs that power is being rearranged as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc angles to lead the government.

But for Palestinians, the machinery of occupation, dispossession and deprivation keeps running. Israeli attacks killed at least 37 people in Gaza in the past week, while in the occupied West Bank, settlers attacked whole villages with little to stop them.

Gaza: Two narratives of daily killing under the “ceasefire”

The past week saw numerous Israeli attacks and killings in Gaza, as military claims of targeting fighters were weighed against accounts of people killed in tents, filling water containers and driving to a wedding photo shoot. According to Gaza’s Ministry of Health, as of November 16, Israel has killed 1,650 Palestinians since the October 2025 “ceasefire”.

On November 12, an Israeli bomb hit the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis. The hospital’s surgery building was struck, killing six people, including surgeon Rizq Abu Shaira, and wounding dozens. The Israeli military said it targeted Hamas’s Khan Younis Brigade commander, Muhammad Abu Ismail, and accused Hamas of running a command centre in the hospital. In the days that followed, the foreign ministers of 18 Arab and Muslim-majority countries condemned the attack as a violation of international humanitarian law.

Beyond the hospital bombing, the Israeli military told Israeli media it had killed 10 Hamas operatives in the past week. Among them was Samir Abu Younis, whom the army named as Hamas’s Rafah Brigade commander, killed in a drone strike in al-Mawasi on November 14, which Hamas confirmed. The strike hit a tent for displaced people , wounding two. Over the weekend, in Jabalia camp, two men were killed in a strike the army said targeted “terrorists”, and a separate strike on a Gaza government security post in al-Mawasi, Rafah, killed two people, according to Wafa.

At the same time, Israeli forces continued to kill Palestinians in circumstances that offered little indication of any military target:

A tank shell hit an apartment in the al-Qastal towers in Deir el-Balah on November 13, where mourners had gathered. Israeli tanks then fired on people fleeing, killing at least three, including 12-year-old Ahmed Abu Daher, and wounding at least 20, according to local activist Hamza al-Masri and Gaza Now.

According to Wafa, a man was killed by a drone on November 11 as he filled water containers on his Gaza City roof. The next day, a driver taking a groom to a wedding photo shoot in Deir el-Balah was killed by Israeli fire.

On November 16, a man was shot dead at displacement tents in Jabalia, while three people, including a child, were separately wounded by gunfire inside a school south of Khan Younis, Wafa reported.

This week, Gaza’s Health Ministry recorded the winter’s first death from hypothermia – a nine-month-old baby – following the devastation of last week’s rains . Israel’s Prime Minister’s Office claimed more than 91,000 tents and 8,200 trucks of winter supplies have been delivered, the Times of Israel reported, and blamed Hamas for the suffering. The United Nations, however, reported this week that aid-truck offloads have fallen about 42 percent after Israel suspended the Egyptian corridor.

The United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy called conditions in Gaza “catastrophic” and urged that 150,000 tents be allowed into the territory.

West Bank: Settler attacks, closures and two pogroms

The most violent olive harvest on record continues in the occupied West Bank, as OCHA counted 410 harvest-related attacks this year as of November 9. The week saw several kinds of attacks by settlers and soldiers unfold repeatedly across the West Bank:

Harvest and land: Residents reported settlers attacking pickers at Deir Istiya, Abu Nujeim, Wadi Saif near Beit Fajjar, Beit Dajan and Deir Jarir. On November 10, dozens of masked settlers attacked Rabbis for Human Rights volunteers and farmers at Qusra, injuring six, the Times of Israel reported. Settlers also bulldozed farmland at Marj Arzal and Sinjil and uprooted olive trees at as-Sawiya, according to Israeli field monitor Jonathan Pollack and local residents.

Arson and vandalism: Settlers burned a Bedouin tent at Deir Qaddis, set a car ablaze in Taybeh while spray-painting “Death to Arabs”, and destroyed beehives at Atara, according to Wafa and Pollack.

Closures and raids: In al-Mughayyir, settlers pitched a tent in a zone closed to Palestinians, and that night, troops sealed the village, raiding a wedding hall and arresting the groom and three guests. Forces also imposed a curfew on Beit Ummar and closed ad-Dhahiriya’s main entrance, Wafa reported.

But in the past week, two settler attacks escalated into full-blown pogroms against Palestinian communities. Late on November 10, more than 50 masked settlers set fire to a scrapyard, a workshop and cars beside homes in al-Lubban Asharqiya, south of Nablus, burning more than 100 vehicles and dozens of olive trees and cutting power. Wafa put the damage from the attack at more than one million shekels ($310,000). On November 12, after soldiers evicted an outpost near Atara, north of Ramallah, settlers smashed four homes and a factory and wrecked at least three cars, injuring more than 10 residents.

The Israeli army evacuated outposts near Burqa, Wadi al-Rakhim and Jalud, and on November 11, police arrested four Israelis over a September attack by settlers on troops escorting a displaced Palestinian family, the Times of Israel reported.

Yet settlers re-established an outpost at Burqa within days, and in Wadi al-Rakhim, south of Yatta, the six-week siege of Yousef Shanaran’s home by settlers continues unimpeded. While soldiers pulled down the settlers’ tent outside Shanaran’s home on November 13, the tent was rebuilt after sunset, according to the family. On November 16, Shanaran told Al Jazeera that settlers had thrown stones at their home throughout the previous night. Soldiers were present, but did nothing. “We are alone,” he declared.

Eisenkot condemns racism, but courts the Haredim

As the occupation continues largely unchecked, early coalition negotiations suggest that a change of government might mean little more than a rearrangement of the political chairs for Palestinians. On November 10, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told the new parliament in a speech Eisenkot called “hate-filled” that Arab-led parties “seek to destroy the Jewish state”, while demanding a Zionist unity government instead of the opposition partnering with the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel.

Meanwhile, Israel’s Channel 12 reported on November 15 that Netanyahu’s chief of staff had given police the tip behind three election-day arrests of activists from Ra’am, one of the Arab-led parties. Israel’s attorney general is probing whether Netanyahu’s office engineered the case to bolster claims that Arab parties stole the vote. Shin Bet chief David Zini also asked to wiretap five Palestinian members of the Israeli parliament, Channel 12 reported. Netanyahu’s office has called the report defamatory.

Eisenkot called the campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel “racist and violent” and said Netanyahu was a threat to Israeli democracy who could not stay “for even one more minute” .

Yet he has ruled out a government with the Arab parties, whose 19 seats would give his bloc 67, above the 61-seat majority threshold.

Instead, the week’s moves point towards Eisenkot working with the ultra-Orthodox: right-wing anti-Netanyahu leader Avigdor Liberman, just approved as chair of the parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee, suggested working with military leaders, the High Court and religious leaders to compromise on any ultra-Orthodox conscription bill, the Times of Israel reported.

articles.title: Guernsey reservoirs get boost but water-saving plea remains
articles.summary: Storms brought the first rise in reservoir levels since June, adding 100 million litres.
articles.body:
Storms Austen and Boelo gave Guernsey reservoirs a short-lived boost, but islanders are still being urged to save water as winter begins.

The storms delivered the first increase in reservoir levels since June, adding 100 million litres, said Guernsey Water.

But it pointed out that reservoirs were still only 70% full, about 2% below the level recorded at the same time last year, 6% below the five-year average and 10% below the decade average.

Guernsey Water operations manager Jon Holt said the recent rain had nudged storage levels in the right direction, but warned "a couple of wet days cannot do the whole job and downpours don't end droughts".

He said sustained rainfall was needed to replenish water used during the summer in the island, which did not see water restrictions imposed.

"Unless there is more sustained rain soon, that boost from the storms will have been used up by the end of November," he said.

"A dry winter would place substantial strain on our supplies next summer and make restrictions more likely."

Guernsey Water is encouraging people to check homes and gardens for leaking taps, pipes and toilets, install a water butt where practical and affordable, and clear leaves and debris from drains and gullies to help rainfall reach reservoirs.

articles.title: Australian builder ordered to pay $269,982 over defects in a Canberra home; appeal court rejects full $200,000 deduction for certifier settlement but allows a limited credit
articles.summary: Two homeowners in Latham, Canberra, took their builder to court over failures to follow approved plans and building standards during construction of their
articles.body: Two homeowners in Latham, Canberra, took their builder to court over failures to follow approved plans and building standards during construction of their home. The Supreme Court found that M Johnson Building Pty Ltd had breached the building contract and ordered it to pay $269,982.66 in damages. The builder appealed, challenging the award for excavation work and arguing that a separate settlement should reduce its liability.According to the Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory, the Court of Appeal confirmed the order requiring the builder to pay $269,982.66 in damages but directed the homeowners to give credit for the relevant portion of the $200,000 settlement received from the building certifier.What caused a home-building dispute over excavation costs in AustraliaThe dispute concerned a residential house in Latham built by M Johnson Building Pty Ltd. The owners, Kate Mary O’Toole and Farooq Ahmed, alleged that the builder had failed to construct the house according to the approved plans and required building standards. They also raised other complaints about defective construction, each framed as a breach of the building contract.At the hearing, the Supreme Court found that the alleged breaches had been established. The builder did not challenge every part of the primary judgment. The $95,746.57 cost of the site cut was not in dispute. The builder argued the contract made the owners responsible for it, relying on a $3,000 siteworks allowance or, alternatively, on landscaping being excluded from the contract. The primary judge rejected the landscaping argument.The judge explained that once the site was excavated to the condition required under the contract, some landscaping might still be needed. However, this did not mean the owners were claiming payment for unrelated landscaping work.They were seeking the cost of completing work that the builder was contractually required to carry out but had left unfinished. The builder also challenged how a separate payment from the building certifier was treated after the owners settled their claim against that company.Unsafe excavation at Latham home leads to dispute over builder’s contractual dutiesOne disputed item involved an inadequate site cut behind the house. The approved plans required the removal of 88 cubic metres of land, but the builder accepted that the excavation had not been carried out as specified. The Supreme Court found that the work breached the contract and had not been completed in a proper and skilful manner.Rectification was assessed at $95,746.57. Engineering experts described the existing excavation as unsafe because of its height and near-vertical formation. They argued that remedial work was necessary to make the site safe. This included reshaping the excavated areas to a safe angle and building retaining walls.The primary judge noted the builder’s concession that he was required to leave the site in a safe condition, in finding the rectification cost reasonable. The Court of Appeal rejected the builder’s argument that the owners were responsible for the cost because it had not been pleaded at trial. In any event, the contract did not support it as no provisional sums were specified, and the excavation was part of the approved plans.Why did an Australian builder challenge damages after a certifier paid $200,000The owners had also sued Capital Certifiers Pty Ltd, the building certifier, but settled that claim shortly before the trial. Under consent orders, the certifier paid $200,000, including costs, on 17 May 2023. The Supreme Court later assessed total damages at $287,084 and ordered the builder to pay $269,982.66. The reduction reflected an agreed apportionment that assigned 85% of responsibility to the builder and 15% to the certifier for shared losses.Some items were outside the certifier’s supervision, leaving the builder wholly responsible for those amounts. The builder argued that the settlement should also reduce the damages payable by it.Court limits compensation deduction to prevent double recoveryThe Court of Appeal agreed that the certifier’s payment had to be considered to prevent the owners receiving double compensation for the same loss. However, it rejected the builder’s request to deduct the entire $200,000 settlement from the damages. The court found that only some losses overlapped between the two claims, while other losses were solely the builder’s responsibility.It confirmed the damages order and directed the owners to give credit for any part of the settlement exceeding $17,100.94 and one-third of their solicitor-client costs up to 20 April 2023. The appeal was allowed in part. The parties were also given 14 days to file submissions on appeal and trial costs.Disclaimer: This article is based on the judgment delivered by the Supreme Court of the Australian Capital Territory, Court of Appeal. The Times of India has not independently verified the construction defects, contractual breaches or costs discussed in the proceedings. The findings and compensation amounts mentioned are based on the court records.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2010, Michigan crews mixed 5% cement-kiln dust into weak soil beneath Waverly Road; four years later, one test hole recorded a CBR of 87.5, versus 17 in untreated soil
articles.summary: Discover how the innovative use of cement-kiln dust has transformed the weak soil conditions beneath Michigan's roads, resulting in significantly improved strength and performance.
articles.body: Soft soil under a road can be a hidden headache for engineers and a bumpy ride for drivers. One possible fix was tested in a 2023 Geotechnics paper by Lawrence Technological University’s Nishantha Bandara and colleagues, funded by the Michigan Department of Transportation. In 2010, crews in Michigan mixed 5% cement-kiln dust into weak soil under Waverly Road. Four years later, one test hole’s California bearing ratio (CBR), a standard soil-strength score, was 87.5 compared to 17 in untreated soil.Why weak soil is a big problem Michigan has a soil problem under many of its roads. The Michigan Department of Transportation says in its Research Spotlight report RC-1635, ‘Performance Evaluation of Subgrade Stabilization with Recycled Materials,’ that as much as 40% of the state has problem soils. The standard fix, as the Geotechnics paper notes, is undercutting. Crews dig out the soft soil and replace it with better material to fill the hole. The authors say that the earthwork here is very large-scale and expensive. This is especially true for southeastern Michigan, which holds much of the population and the road network. The soil can also be made stronger with cement and lime. However, both of them are rather expensive as they are manufactured materials with other uses. That's why the researchers turned to an industrial byproduct instead.How the dust was used Cement kiln dust is a waste product from the cement industry. On Waverly Road in Ingham County, built in 2010, crews mixed it into a 12-inch (about 30 centimetre) layer of weak clay using 5% of the soil’s weight. The paper suggests kiln dust may be a cheaper alternative to cement or lime. However, it hasn't taken off, partly because there is little test data. In lab work, the team found that 4% to 8% was best for clay soils, and 5% fell in that zone. Waverly Road was one of the four road sites in Michigan and Ohio that the team tested years after it was built. Two sites used cement kiln dust, and the other two used lime kiln dust.What the tests showedIn November 2014, the team tested the strength of the soil. They made small holes in the road and put a rod with a conical point in the ground by dropping an 8 kg weight on it. The number of blows needed was a measure of the strength of each layer. Engineers used that figure to calculate the CBR score. At the time, there was no visible damage on the road. In one test hole, the treated layers scored 87.5, and the untreated soil below scored 17. That's about five times stronger. On average, the thickness of the treated layer was 10.5 inches, falling below the target of 12 inches.The catch behind the numbers The result isn't as straightforward as it might seem. Of the four test holes on Waverly Road, only one showed any sign of treatment and it received a score of 87.5. The authors used that hole’s values for the site because the other three scores were poor and inconsistent. The possible reasons included the poor mixing of the dust and wet conditions that lasted too long. However, the picture improved at all four sites. The paper reports that after 4 to 6 years of exposure, all three cement kiln dust test sections (two at I-75/I-96 and one on Waverly Road) were still twice as durable as the soil below. The department's spotlight makes it clear that the recycled materials across the entire site could cost two to three times less than undercutting. However, undercutting may end up winning out for small spot repairs. So, kiln dust is promising, but good mixing is also important.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Leonid meteor shower 2026: How and when to see the peak
articles.summary: The Leonid meteor shower, known for its bright and fast meteors, is set to peak on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The Leonid meteor shower reaches its peak on Tuesday night, giving UK sky gazers their best chance to see it this year.

The celestial spectacle runs until 30 November, but the greatest activity is expected on the night of Tuesday 17 November, into the early hours of Wednesday.

There could be the chance to spot up to 10-15 meteors per hour.

The shower is made up of dust particles from the Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which leaves a trail of debris as it follows its path around the Sun.

These particles enter the Earth's atmosphere at up to 44 miles (71km) per second, meaning these streaks of light are the fastest meteors in the sky.

Experts advise finding a safe, dark location away from sources of light pollution such as street lights.

The meteors will be visible with the naked eye, with no binoculars or telescope required.

However, giving your eyes some time to adapt to the dark, perhaps 20 or 30 minutes, will give you the best chance of spotting them.

A wide open space is the best place to be, giving a full view of the night sky.

Meteors could be visible anywhere but the Leonids' radiant, the point from which they seem to appear, will, as the name suggests, be around the head of the constellation Leo, meaning this is the best part of the sky to focus your gaze. Leo does not rise until around midnight, so the best time to look is after midnight and in the hours before dawn.

As with all celestial spectacles, clear skies will be a must.

What will the weather be like on Tuesday night?

Viewing conditions could be particularly good around the peak. The Moon will set at around 23:30 GMT on Tuesday, meaning its reflected light is less likely to spoil the view in the hours after midnight.

The best chance of seeing the Leonids will be in the far north of Scotland, including Orkney and Shetland, where cloud is expected to be well broken with only a small chance of a passing shower.

Parts of Northern Ireland, Wales, the Midlands and southern England will also have clear spells at times but there will be periods of cloudier weather and some splashes of rain.

In Northern Ireland, the Midlands and North Wales, the best chance of clear breaks will be earlier in the night.

Much of Scotland away from the far north, and northern England, will have limited opportunities. A few places may see the odd gap in the cloud but for most it will be cloudy and damp.

articles.title: South Korea cheating scandal: Are AI smart glasses a threat to exams?
articles.summary: A student with near-perfect scores on two tests has confessed to using artificial intelligence.
articles.body:
South Korea is racing to fix potential security gaps in upcoming exams after a top scorer on a national test admitted to using artificial intelligence to cheat.

Prime Minister Han Seok-sook called an emergency meeting on Monday, where the education minister was tasked with enforcing new anti-cheating measures ahead of high-pressure annual national college entrance exams known as “Suneung” this week.

The scandal began after speculation mounted over a student’s near-perfect scores on two separate exams that contained hundreds of questions.

Now, authorities say cheaters using high-tech gadgets could face criminal prosecution if caught.

In a statement last week, the prime minister said her government “will prepare thoroughly in advance and closely oversee the process until the very end to ensure the college entrance exam is conducted fairly and stably”.

In a video published online on Sunday, the student, wearing a mask, admitted to using a miniature camera and AI during the exam for aspiring tax accountants.

Identified as Han Won-seok by South Korean media, the student had taken exams in April and July and answered nearly all questions correctly, raising concerns about potential cheating and prompting investigations.

“I cheated using electronic devices and generative AI. My passing the exam with the top score was not the result of fair effort,” he said in the YouTube video.

He explained that he took photos of the exam questions with the mini camera and sent them to an AI tool. He also said he used a smartphone.

The student said he had submitted a written confession detailing his process to the Seoul police. He also warned future cheaters to reconsider.

“I’m going to tell the investigators everything, so I hope you don’t think that you won’t get caught,” he said.

The prime minister has called for his results to be invalidated and for him to be banned from national examinations.

The case has triggered uproar in South Korea, where notoriously difficult tests determine students’ life trajectories.

Many spend much of their high school years preparing to pass entrance exams, particularly the Suneung, or the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), which lasts for nearly 10 hours. Flights are suspended to allow total concentration during the exam’s English listening segment, and drivers are asked not to honk for the half-an-hour it takes.

On Monday, Minister of Education Choi Kyo-jin said new measures would be instituted, including the inspection of glasses worn by students.

He also said cheating with smart devices could carry criminal punishment.

The ministry has in recent weeks said it would pursue criminal prosecution for cheating during the annual college entrance exam. It also said it was seeking to extend the one-year exam ban for those caught using smart devices to three years.

There will be “a thorough inspection of all glasses in each test session to ensure a fair and safe testing environment”, the minister said.

The case has revealed the risks AI could pose to exams as smart gadgets make cheating easier, and as authorities appear to be playing catch-up on how the new tools are being deployed.

It could especially affect Asian countries like South Korea, reputed for conducting arduous exams with strict anti-cheating protocols meant to ensure fairness.

Reports of students using AI-powered smart glasses that allow them to look at questions and see responses immediately are becoming common.

A South Korean education official said students likely enter AI prompts beforehand and activate the glasses during tests.

Early iterations of smart glasses featured identifiable cameras in their frames, but the devices are increasingly inconspicuous, making them difficult to detect.

In October, three students in South Korea were caught using smart glasses during tests at universities in Seoul.

In Taiwan, the National Taiwan University disqualified a student in June from medical school entrance exams for allegedly using AI smart glasses to cheat.

Authorities are promising stricter measures. In July, South Korea’s education authorities banned smart glasses from exams and said they will deploy one dedicated person per 1,312 CSAT test sites to inspect eyewear.

Seoul is also mulling introducing technology to detect advanced gadgets on students, including radio-frequency detectors. Public Wi-Fi, officials say, could be disabled at test sites too.

Chinese authorities are likewise tightening measures for the competitive college entry, or Gaokao, exam by equipping testing sites with intelligent security gates to detect smart glasses and other gadgets.

articles.title: Vladimir Putin’s prized bridge is partially destroyed in Ukrainian strike
articles.summary: A key bridge connecting the occupied Crimean Peninsula with mainland Russia suffered significant damage Tuesday, a landmark blow to President Vladimir Putin.
articles.body: A key bridge connecting the occupied Crimean Peninsula with mainland Russia suffered significant damage Tuesday, a landmark blow to President Vladimir Putin. Videos and photos geolocated by NBC News show the partial destruction of the strategically important Kerch Bridge, with one section collapsed into the water. Russian authorities confirmed that the structure had been damaged shutting down traffic and that an emergency government meeting had been called after back-to-back attacks starting Monday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack “an unprecedented operation in response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure.” He shared video in a post on X that appears to show a missile approaching the section of the bridge that was later seen damaged. The SBU, Ukraine’s Security Service, said in a separate statement that one of the bridge’s metal arches and the road span beneath it were completely destroyed, and the railway section was also damaged, using a “wide range of Ukrainian-made weapons.” Dealing critical damage to the bridge is a significant coup for Kyiv, as it reels from deadly Russian attacks on its own vital infrastructure, including two bridges in the capital. The damage to his signature achievement is likely to sour Putin’s mood ahead of the extraordinary meeting this week with President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Putin made the construction of the bridge his flagship project, meant to solidify Russian dominance over Crimea, the peninsula he illegally annexed in 2014. Beyond its symbolic value, the road and rail bridge has served as a vital supply route for the Russian military. Asked how Putin reacted to the attacks, his spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a plan will be drawn up to restore the bridge. “There is, in fact, no doubt that the bridge will be restored. And it will be even better than before,” Peskov said. The Russian Transport Ministry said Tuesday all train and vehicular traffic on the bridge had been suspended after the second attack overnight. The first attack was reported early Monday. “Experts are assessing the damage,” the ministry said. Russia’s Investigative Committee said Tuesday it had opened a criminal case into what it called “a terrorist act” in connection with the bridge attacks, confirming there was “damage to the structure.” Zelenskyy said the bridge attack was the seventh stage of an operation that lasted several weeks. He said his forces destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other targets “on the way to the final objective.” “Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region,” he said. “We are restoring our infrastructure. But we are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began.” The 12-mile road and rail bridge, which Moscow says is the longest in Europe, has served as a key supply and transportation route into Crimea from Russia, although Russian troops also rely on a land corridor through Russian-controlled territory in southern Ukraine. The bridge was “the main military crossing from the territory of Russia into our Ukrainian Crimea,” Zelenskyy said Tuesday. The bridge, which cost about $2.7 billion, is also an important transportation artery for civilians. The Russian Transportation Ministry said that in the five years since the bridge opened to traffic in 2018, nearly 24 million vehicles have traveled in both directions. The Russian-installed head of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, asked residents and visitors to refrain from traveling in the direction of the bridge after the attacks. Two people were killed in a drone strike in a district close to the bridge, he said. Some rail traffic resumed Tuesday, he later added, as he said passengers without vehicles could also use ferries to get across. The Russian-installed governor of the Crimean city of Sevastopol, Mikhail Razvozhayev, assured residents the city’s supplies would not be affected, and warned against spreading panic. Authorities were working on developing “alternative logistics solutions” for people who need to return home or continue their journeys, he said. The bridge has also served as an important gateway for Russia between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea for ships carrying grain, oil and liquefied petroleum gas. The passage under the bridge is crucial for shipping through the Sea of Azov, and the collapse of one of its sections could at least temporarily block this route. Black Sea shipping has been severely disrupted for months as the drone war expanded into its waters. “This bottleneck was previously used against Ukraine, but now it’s a problem for the Russians. It’s unknown how long it will take to remove the debris and reopen the channel,” Emil Kastehelmi, a military analyst with the Finland-based Black Bird Group, wrote in an analysis on X. The strikes are part of an intensifying exchange between the two sides, hitting critical infrastructure despite the recent uptick in diplomatic activity and American pressure to try and settle the conflict. U.S.-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates last week ended without any significant breakthroughs. Authorities in Kyiv said Tuesday that two of its main bridges were damaged and closed as the result of overnight Russian attacks, which they said killed two people. The attacks were acknowledged by the Russian Defense Ministry, which said the spans were being used to transport military cargo. Meanwhile, energy officials also reported new strikes on Ukraine’s power grid across eight regions of the country, as cities throughout Ukraine suffer water and power outages. Ukraine has, meanwhile, ramped up the number of drones it has been flying into Russian territory in recent days. The Russian Defense Ministry said Tuesday that more than 1,400 Ukrainian drones were shot down, the biggest attack since the war began. It came a day after the previous largest attack. The Kerch Bridge has come under several major Ukrainian attacks since the full-scale invasion, including from a truck bomb in 2022, and from Ukrainian naval drones in 2023. Putin has previously described the bridge as a “symbol of Crimea’s reunification with Russia and an opportunity for the peninsula’s development.” The new Ukrainian strikes showcase “Russia’s inability to defend strategic objects that are critical both for the Russian economy and military logistics,” according to analysis by the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War. “The road bridge won’t be repaired during this war,” Kastehelmi wrote. “The steel arch is a large element which had to be lifted into position in 2017 and the structural damage to the foundations can be severe. Ukraine has achieved a victory with both concrete and symbolic implications.”

articles.title: Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo is undergoing care after eating a hat
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Zoo says its beloved hippo Fiona, who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a hat.
articles.body: CINCINNATI — The Cincinnati Zoo says its beloved hippo Fiona, who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat that got into her enclosure. Zoo veterinarians and staff are monitoring Fiona and working to help her pass the hat, the zoo said in a statement Monday. “Her care team is cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self,” the zoo said. The cap got into Fiona’s habitat after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a small opening above the area’s viewing windows, said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley. Fiona was born six weeks premature in January 2017, and her fight to survive grabbed international attention. She initially couldn’t stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds (13.2 kilograms) at birth, 25 pounds (11.3 kilograms) less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species. Fans followed her progress online, and she became so popular that books were written about her. She also inspired a line of beer, all sorts of clothing and an ice cream flavor. One couple even got engaged in front of her exhibit, with Fiona getting into the picture while underwater in the background.
